name: Civil Engineering Technician
description: Civil engineering technicians support design and construction — drawings and quantities, surveying, materials testing and the site inspection that catches what was built wrong. ⚠ 64,900 employed nationally, and the Florida programme that carries its name is the smallest on this site: eight institutions, 16 credentials.
credentialNote: ⚠ No licence governs technician work, and the education bar is lower than in the other technician occupations here — 30% a post-secondary certificate, 28% some college, 21% an associate degree. ⚠⚠ What matters more is WHERE the training is: only eight Florida institutions award the named degree, so the practical route is construction technology, drafting and surveying courses, plus the short materials-testing certifications (concrete, soils, asphalt) that inspection work actually requires. ⚠ And compare the civil ENGINEERING degree deliberately: it is offered at nine institutions — more than this programme — and under s. 471.013 it reaches a PE in four years of experience rather than six, which matters in civil practice more than in any other discipline.
bodyHtml:
What the work actually is

O*NET: apply theory and principles of civil engineering in planning, designing and overseeing construction and maintenance of structures and facilities under the direction of engineering staff or physical scientists. The tasks are the project's paperwork and its checking — calculate dimensions, square footage, profile and component specifications and material quantities; read and review project blueprints and structural specifications; draft detailed dimensional drawings and design layouts; inspect project site and evaluate contractor work to detect design malfunctions and ensure conformance to design specifications and applicable codes.

⚠ Inspection is the part that carries responsibility. A civil technician on site is often the person who notices that what is being built is not what was drawn — and saying so early is the whole value of the role.

Projected need

O*NET, on federal projections: 64,900 employed (2024), growth “slower than average (1% to 2%)”, 5,500 openings a year, median wages $64,950 (2025). Education: 30% a post-secondary certificate, 28% some college, 21% an associate degree — notably lower expectations than the industrial or mechanical technician occupations.

⚠⚠⚠ The smallest programme on this site — and what to do about it

Eight Florida public institutions award in civil engineering technology, and they awarded 16 credentials in 2023. For an occupation with 5,500 openings a year nationally, that is close to nothing.

⚠ The work is real; the programme name is not where Florida trains for it. The courses that actually prepare people are filed under construction technology, drafting and surveying, and they are widely available: introduction to structures at nine institutions, construction estimating at nine, blueprint reading and construction drafting at eight, AutoCAD at nine.

⚠ So build the qualification from those, and ask two questions of any college: which of these courses it carries, and what they articulate into. ⚠⚠ And compare the civil ENGINEERING degree honestly — nine institutions award it, which is more than award this technology programme, and it opens the PE route that a technology degree lengthens by two years.

Necessary skills

  • Drawings, in both directions — reading a construction set properly, and producing clean drafted work in AutoCAD or Civil 3D.
  • Quantities and estimating. Calculating material and cost from a drawing is a daily task and a hireable skill on its own.
  • Surveying fundamentals — levels, layout and coordinates. ⚠ Only two or three Florida institutions carry the surveying courses, so this is often learned on the job.
  • Materials and testing — concrete, asphalt, soils, and the inspection routines that go with them.
  • Documentation and site communication. Daily reports, RFIs, and telling a contractor that something is wrong in a way that gets it fixed.

Advice

  • ⚠ Do not plan on the named degree without checking it is near you — eight institutions statewide. Build from construction technology, drafting and surveying courses instead if it is not.
  • Learn Civil 3D as well as AutoCAD if you can. It is what Florida civil consultancies run on, and it is frequently the thing that gets a technician hired.
  • Get on a site. Inspection and materials-testing work is where technicians are genuinely needed, and testing certifications (concrete, soils, asphalt) are short, cheap and respected.
  • Florida's work is specific — transportation for FDOT and its consultants, stormwater and drainage, coastal and port projects, and the inspection load that follows every hurricane season.
  • ⚠ Compare the civil engineering degree deliberately. It is offered more widely than this programme, and the licence timetable is four years rather than six — which matters in civil practice more than in any other discipline.
